articles.title: The Briefing Room - Has France become ungovernable? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: After mass protests and violence, what will persuade the French to accept economic reform?
articles.body: Will the French accept that changes need to be made to fix their ailing economy? Political paralysis and a debt crisis has led to 5 prime ministers in the last two years. Every attempt at fixing the economic problems is met with outrage and protest. Saturday 17th October 2026 saw some of the worst protests in years, with peaceful demonstrations over the cost of living and school funding descending into an 'apocalyptic hell'. 500 police officers were injured in the violence, 1,500 shops were damaged and an historic 19th century city hall was burnt to the ground in the mass disorder that ensued. But there are some serious economic issues that must be faced head on. France's borrowing costs have just hit a 26 year high, signalling they are not trusted to manage their growing debt. Public spending in France is higher than in many other European countries and a big part of that bill is pensions. Raising the pension age would save the state much needed money but proposals to do so were met with outrage and put on hold. So, has France become ungovernable? Guests: Sophie Pedder, Paris bureau chief, The Economist Victor Mallet, Financial Times, author of Far-Right France: Le Pen, Bardella and the Future of Europe Agnes Poiriet, UK editor, L'Express Producers: Ben Carter, Phoebe Keane, Kirsteen Knight

articles.title: BBC Inside Science - Is there time on Mars? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: A Japanese spacecraft could become the first ever to bring Martian samples back to Earth.
articles.body: The first ever spacecraft to bring Martian samples back to Earth has launched from Japan. However, before the spacecraft returns from Phobos in 2031 there are many complex challenges that lie ahead, leaving an anxious 5 year wait for the scientists involved. To help us understand just how ambitious a feat of engineering the Mars Moons eXploration mission is Tom Whipple is joined by Naomi Murdoch, research director at ISAE-SUPAERO. What is it like to carry out scientific research when your work might lead to you being publicly cancelled or reviled? For the next few weeks, we are going to be hearing from finalists of Sense about Science’s John Maddox Prize, this week neuropsychologist Professor Sallie Baxendale discusses what it is like to continue their scientific endeavours despite being met with hostility. Plus managing editor of New Scientist Penny Sarchet brings Tom a round-up of the science news you might have missed. Produced in partnership with The Open University. Presenter: Tom Whipple Producer: Alex Mansfield, Keiran Manetta-Jones Editor: Martin Smith

articles.title: Travelers are screaming at 'Obsession' on planes. Is watching horror in flight rude?
articles.summary: Travelers watching "Obsession" on planes are sharing their startled reactions online. Here's what etiquette experts say about choosing inflight entertainment...
articles.body:
Horror fans flocked to theaters to see the smash horror hit Obsession . Now, some people are watching it on a plane — and it's startling passengers.

Multiple airlines now have Obsession available on demand, and it seems many people are choosing to check out the movie for the first time on the flight. One video, posted on Instagram on Sept. 17, shows a person filming the flier in front of them as they watch the movie.

During one of the film's most famous jump scares, the traveler is heard yelping and waking a baby in the process.

A second viral video , posted on Oct. 11 on TikTok, shows a woman recording her mom watching Obsession on a plane, only for her to scream at the very same part.

On Letterboxd, a social media site where people share film reviews, people have also talked about taking Obsession to the sky.

One person said , "Crazy ass movie to watch on a flight — my 4-5 loud gasps were not amusing to my neighbors…" Another added , "Kind of an insane movie to let people watch on a plane but at least I finally got to see it?"

People have thoughts about this on Reddit too. One person wrote, "Literally just happened to me. I didn't think they would allow a movie like this on the plane."

Someone even started a Reddit thread asking if they should watch Obsession on a plane in the first place, asking if it's too violent to view in mixed company.

Obsession is hardly the only content people have watched on planes that has stirred controversy. In 2019, a viral internet debate sparked after a redditor asked if they were wrong for not wanting to turn off Game of Thrones because a mother sitting with a child behind them was concerned that her young son could see the sex and violence onscreen.

But are there any official etiquette rules about what you should or should not watch on an airplane, so as not to disturb your fellow passengers? Etiquette experts tell Yahoo Travel that being thoughtful can go a long way.

Diane Gottsman, etiquette expert and owner of The Protocol School of Texas , tells Yahoo Travel that it's completely fine to watch a film provided in the inflight entertainment system, such as Obsession . However, you may want to look around and see who is sitting near you who could glance at your screen. While adults can distract themselves from a screen with a book or movie of their own, a young child may not be able to do so, and may be disturbed by the content.

But just because you're near a child doesn't mean you can't watch a scary movie. Anne Chertoff, chief operating officer of Beaumont Etiquette , tells Yahoo Travel that if you are concerned about a child viewing the screen, you can give the parents a heads-up first. "Just say, 'Look, I'm putting on this horror movie, and some of the scenes may be scary if the child saw it,'" she explains. That way, the parents can distract a child from your screen if necessary.

She notes that if you're bringing your own content on a plane, such as a movie you downloaded on an iPad or laptop, you can use a privacy protector on your screen. And always make sure you're wearing headphones at a volume no one around you can hear as well.

Etiquette expert Thomas Farley tells Yahoo Travel that the bigger concern with scary movies on a plane is how you react. If you know you jump, scream or yelp when, say, a monster pops up onscreen, you should probably skip watching one in flight.

"I'd be embarrassed if I screamed out loud," Farley says. "But I'd be very concerned about doing so in a way that might disturb passengers."

articles.title: Segurança eleições Roraima: Mil policiais atuam no 2º turno | G1
articles.standfirst: Efetivo será distribuído em 355 locais de votação da capital e do interior. PM também usará plataforma digital para acompanhar a operação em tempo real.
articles.summary: Com mil policiais em 355 locais, a segurança das eleições em Roraima terá monitoramento digital em tempo real durante a votação do 2º turno.
articles.body:
Mais de mil policiais militares vão atuar nos 355 locais de votação de Roraima no segundo turno das Eleições 2026 , marcado para este domingo (25). A operação terá reforço no policiamento ostensivo e preventivo na capital Boa Vista e nos 14 municípios do interior .

Eleitores de Roraima vão às urnas no domingo apenas para votar para presidente e vice-presidente da República . Isso porque a eleição para governador foi definida ainda no primeiro turno, em 4 de outubro, quando Arthur Henrique (PL) foi eleito .

O detalhes da operação, chamada de " Eleições Seguras ", foram fechados em reunião nesta quarta-feira (21) no Quartel do Comando-Geral (QCG) da PM, em Boa Vista.

O subcomandante-geral da PM, coronel Igo Mayko Evangelista, afirmou que a corporação está preparada para atuar com foco na prevenção de ocorrências e na manutenção da ordem pública.

"Nossa população pode ficar tranquila. São mais de mil policiais atuando, tanto nos 14 municípios do interior quanto na capital, Boa Vista, garantindo a segurança para que todos possam exercer seu direito ao voto de forma tranquila e segura", afirmou.

Policiais militares prontos para atuação em Roraima — Foto: PMRR/Divulgação

Na operação, a PM informou que vai utilizar a plataforma digital Operar PMRR , desenvolvida pelo Departamento de Tecnologia da Informação (DTI) e pelo Gabinete de Planejamento Estratégico (Gape). A ferramenta foi usada pela primeira vez no primeiro turno e ainda está em fase de testes.

O sistema permite que os policiais consultem o mapa da operação, verifiquem os locais de atuação, registrem o início e o fim do serviço, comuniquem ocorrências e solicitem apoio operacional.

A plataforma também possibilita a comunicação direta entre os policiais, os comandos da operação e a central de acompanhamento.

articles.title: UFU recebe autorização para implantar curso de Medicina em Ituiutaba | G1
articles.standfirst: O ministro da Educação esteve em Uberlândia na quarta-feira (21) e assinou a portaria que autoriza a criação do curso de Medicina no campus da Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU) em Ituiutaba.
articles.summary: O ministro da Educação esteve em Uberlândia na quarta-feira (21) e assinou a portaria que autoriza a criação do curso de Medicina no Campus Pontal.
articles.body:
Cerimônia contou com a presença de lideranças regionais e apoiadores — Foto: Ismael Cristiano/TV Integração

A Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU) deu mais um passo para a implantação do curso de Medicina em Ituiutaba . Em cerimônia realizada na quarta-feira (21), o ministro da Educação, Leonardo Barchini, assinou a portaria que autoriza oficialmente a criação do curso no Campus Pontal.

Além da portaria, também foi assinado um termo de compromisso que garante recursos para a universidade concluir a estrutura necessária para o início das atividades.

Segundo o ministro, o Governo Federal destinará mais R$ 10 milhões para aquisição de equipamentos e adequações no campus. Antes disso, um laboratório de simulação considerado essencial para a graduação já havia sido construído com recursos de uma emenda parlamentar.

"Nós já tivemos uma emenda com o laboratório de R$ 6 milhões e teremos mais R$ 10 milhões para os equipamentos que estão faltando e para as adequações que estão faltando. É a retomada de investimentos na rede federal. No campus da UFU em Ituiutaba já foi construído o laboratório de simulação, fundamental para o início do curso de Medicina", afirmou Leonardo Barchini.

Os R$ 6 milhões investidos na construção dos laboratórios foram destinados por meio de emenda parlamentar articulada pelo deputado estadual Elismar Prado.

Segundo o parlamentar, a assinatura da portaria era a etapa que faltava para oficializar a criação do curso e permitir o avanço dos processos para a seleção dos primeiros estudantes.

"Os laboratórios estão prontos e é o requisito fundamental para poder iniciar o curso. Faltava o MEC assinar a portaria para a criação do curso oficialmente, para poder anunciar o edital para o primeiro vestibular", disse.

Com a autorização formalizada, a UFU inicia agora os trâmites administrativos para abertura das vagas. A previsão da universidade é lançar, ao longo de 2027, o edital do primeiro processo seletivo. Serão oferecidas 60 vagas por ano.

De acordo com a vice-reitora da UFU, Catarina Machado, o cronograma prevê ampla divulgação do edital antes do início das aulas.

"A gente tem ainda um tempo de elaboração desse edital, de divulgação, porque ele precisa ser bastante divulgado na região. A partir daí, teremos os selecionados para começar o curso, provavelmente no segundo semestre, se tudo correr dentro do previsto. Segundo semestre do ano que vem, 2027", explicou.

Laboratório de simulação para o curso de Medicina — Foto: Cedidas/Elismar Prado

Projeto foi discutido por mais de uma década

As discussões para implantação do curso de Medicina no campus da UFU em Ituiutaba começaram em 2014, mas ficaram sem avanços por vários anos.

O projeto voltou a ser discutido em 2023 e, três anos depois, alcançou uma das etapas mais importantes com a autorização oficial do MEC.

Segundo a prefeita de Ituiutaba, Leandra Guedes, o município já investiu mais de R$ 48 milhões para receber os estudantes durante as atividades práticas.

"Ituiutaba, que é uma cidade polo, com certeza vai ser o divisor de águas para a gente poder realmente transformar a saúde da nossa região. Já investimos mais de R$ 48 milhões na atenção básica para que esses estudantes possam ter os seus estágios dentro das nossas estruturas", afirmou.

Em abril de 2026 , a UFU previu o início do curso de Medicina em Ituiutaba para o segundo semestre de 2026. Na época, a universidade informou que a implantação dependia da autorização oficial do Ministério da Educação (MEC) e da conclusão das etapas estruturais necessárias para a graduação.

O Campus Pontal, na ocasião, já vinha recebendo investimentos para adequação de laboratórios e demais espaços acadêmicos voltados à formação médica, além das articulações junto ao governo federal para viabilizar a autorização definitiva do curso.

Com a assinatura da portaria nesta quarta-feira (21), a expectativa agora é pela publicação do edital do vestibular e pela definição do cronograma para ingresso da primeira turma.

Campus Pontal da UFU, em Ituiutaba, receberá curso de Medicina — Foto: Milton Santos/Dirco

articles.title: À procura de casal de sucuris, fotógrafo tem surpresa em rio de Bonito | G1
articles.standfirst: Imagens mostram animais de grande porte em trecho do rio Sucuri, em Bonito. O fotógrafo Marauan Monteiro relata surpresa ao localizar as serpentes durante o trabalho de campo.
articles.summary: Imagens feitas na manhã de ontem mostram animais de grande porte em trecho de ecoturismo. O fotógrafo relata surpresa ao localizar os répteis durante o trabalho de campo.
articles.body:
À procura de um casal de sucuris, o fotógrafo Marauan Monteiro subiu um drone e acabou encontrando três cobras gigantes próximas umas das outras no Rio Sucuri, em Bonito , no interior de Mato Grosso do Sul, na manhã desta quarta-feira (21). Veja vídeo acima.

O flagrante foi feito durante um trabalho de registro da fauna local e mostra as serpentes de grande porte próximas às águas cristalinas do rio.

Marauan Monteiro relata que foi ao local após receber avisos sobre a presença de cobras na área. Inicialmente, a expectativa era encontrar um casal em período de reprodução em um ponto específico do rio.

Sucuris em rio cristalino de Bonito (MS). — Foto: Maruan Monteiro/Arquivo Pessoal

Ao subir o equipamento, o fotógrafo localizou a primeira cobra de grande porte e recém alimentada. Em seguida, após conversar com os guias da atração, descobriu que havia mais répteis nas imediações, totalizando três cobras na mesma região.

"Na hora que vi, gelou o corpo. Uma sensação de medo com gratidão, pois, por mais longe que ela estivesse, era fascinante ver um animal daquele tamanho de drone. Nunca tinha visto uma cena tão incrível como aquela."

Sucuri gigante após refeição em rio cristalino de Bonito (MS). — Foto: Maruan Monteiro/Arquivo Pessoal

O profissional já havia feito imagens semelhantes anteriormente, mas destaca que os registros anteriores mostravam animais debilitados. Encontrar espécimes gigantes e saudáveis no Rio Sucuri marcou a carreira do fotógrafo, que reforça o fascínio pela biodiversidade sul-mato-grossense.

“Se pudesse ia todo dia lá gravar elas.”

Sucuri se rasteja após refeição. — Foto: Maruan Monteiro

*Estagiária sob supervisão de José Câmara.

articles.title: Rubel: quem é o cantor em polêmica com Nikolas Ferreira? | G1
articles.standfirst: Artista ganhou projeção com músicas como 'Quando Bate Aquela Saudade' e 'Partilhar'; deputado diz que Rubel pediu retirada de áudio de vídeo com críticas ao governo Lula.
articles.summary: Rubel, dono do sucesso 'Partilhar', é citado por Nikolas Ferreira de remover áudio de vídeo crítico ao governo Lula. Conheça a trajetória e as obras do artista.
articles.body:
O cantor Rubel chega a Campo Grande para sua turnê “Beleza. Rubel e Violão”. — Foto: Reprodução

O cantor e compositor Rubel virou um dos assuntos mais comentados nas redes sociais após o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira o acusar de ter derrubado o áudio de um vídeo sobre o Nordeste , em que fazia críticas ao governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT)

A gravação usava como trilha a música Grão de Areia, de Rubel com Xande de Pilares e participação do sanfoneiro Mestrinho. Nikolas responsabilizou o artista pela retirada do áudio e o acusou de tentar silenciar os nordestinos.

Vídeo publicado por Nikolas Ferreira com entrevistas de moradores da Bahia sobre ações do governo do PT na região. — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/nikolasferreiradm

A Meta, empresa responsável pelo Instagram, confirmou que o áudio foi removido após uma reivindicação de direitos autorais. O g1 apurou que a solicitação partiu do cantor Rubel.

A polêmica fez o nome do artista ganhar destaque na internet. No entanto, Rubel já tinha uma trajetória consolidada na música brasileira, com quatro álbuns de estúdio e três indicações ao Grammy Latino.

Rubel Brisolla nasceu em Volta Redonda, no Sul Fluminense, e cresceu no Rio de Janeiro. O cantor começou a estudar violão ainda criança e, na adolescência, integrou uma banda formada por amigos.

Apesar do interesse pela música, ele cursou Cinema na Pontifícia Universidade Católica do Rio de Janeiro (PUC-Rio). Durante um intercâmbio em Austin, no Texas, nos Estados Unidos, voltou a se dedicar à composição e começou a escrever as canções que dariam origem ao primeiro álbum.

Lançado em 2013, o álbum Pearl foi disponibilizado na internet e ganhou público de forma independente. O disco inclui a música Quando Bate Aquela Saudade, que se tornou um dos principais sucessos do artista e ajudou a ampliar sua projeção nacional.

'Partilhar' e as indicações ao Grammy Latino

Em 2018, Rubel lançou Casas, segundo álbum de estúdio, com participações de artistas como Emicida e Rincon Sapiência. O trabalho marcou uma ampliação das referências musicais do cantor, combinando elementos da MPB com gêneros como rap, hip-hop e R&B.

Uma das faixas de destaque do disco foi Partilhar, que ganhou uma versão com a dupla Anavitória e integrou a trilha sonora de novela.

O álbum Casas recebeu uma indicação ao Grammy Latino de 2018, na categoria Melhor Álbum de Rock ou Música Alternativa em Língua Portuguesa.

Em 2023, Rubel lançou o projeto duplo As Palavras, Vol. 1 & 2, que reúne parcerias com nomes como Milton Nascimento, Liniker, Luedji Luna, Tim Bernardes, Xande de Pilares e integrantes do grupo Bala Desejo. O trabalho também foi indicado ao Grammy Latino, na categoria Melhor Álbum de Pop Contemporâneo em Língua Portuguesa.

Em 2025, o artista lançou Beleza. Mas agora a gente faz o que com isso?, indicado ao Grammy Latino na categoria Melhor Álbum de Música Popular Brasileira/Música Afro Portuguesa Brasileira. Com isso, Rubel chegou à terceira indicação ao prêmio.

Rubel — Foto: Bruna Sussekind / Divulgação

A discussão começou na terça-feira (20), quando Nikolas publicou nas redes sociais um vídeo intitulado “O Nordeste que foi esquecido”. A gravação reúne depoimentos de moradores da região sobre dificuldades financeiras, segurança e acesso a serviços, com críticas ao governo Lula.

O vídeo usava um trecho instrumental de Grão de Areia, música gravada por Rubel em parceria com Xande de Pilares e com participação de Mestrinho. Depois da publicação, o áudio foi retirado do Instagram.

Nikolas afirmou que Rubel teria acionado a gravadora Sony para retirar a música da publicação. O deputado também criticou o posicionamento político do cantor, que já declarou apoio a Lula, e o acusou de tentar impedir que os moradores do Nordeste expressassem suas opiniões.

Xande de Pilares também se manifestou sobre o caso e explicou que a autorização para o uso da composição em conteúdos digitais depende dos titulares dos direitos autorais.

articles.title: Aulão na Rede 2026: entenda a evolução da sustentabilidade  | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto da Rede Amazônica divulga vídeos com dicas para o Enem, vestibulares e outros exames.
articles.summary: Projeto da Rede Amazônica divulga vídeos com dicas para o Enem, vestibulares e outros exames.
articles.body:
Diariamente, os telejornais da Rede Amazônica disponibilizam videoaulas do projeto "Aulão na Rede" , que reúne dicas de professores para estudantes que se preparam para o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem). Nessa quarta-feira (21), o professor de geografia Marcelo Dores explica a evolução histórica do conceito de sustentabilidade e do desenvolvimento sustentável.

Na aula, o professor explica que as primeiras discussões sobre o tema ocorreram durante a Guerra Fria e eram marcadas por acusações entre países. Nos anos 1980, o Relatório Brundtland consolidou o conceito de desenvolvimento sustentável (assista acima) .

Marcelo Dores também destaca o Protocolo de Kyoto, firmado em 1997, e as conferências Rio+10 e Rio+20, que contribuíram para estabelecer compromissos e metas ambientais globais.

Os vídeos do "Aulão na Rede" de 2026 são exibidos diariamente nos telejornais da Rede Amazônica desde 12 de outubro e trazem revisões de conteúdos e dicas para estudantes que estão na reta final de preparação para as provas.

A iniciativa reúne professores de diversas áreas para revisar conteúdos cobrados nas principais provas do país.

articles.title: MPE reforça pedido para que PF investigue deputado e blogueira em RR | G1
articles.standfirst: Promotoria aponta cinco possíveis crimes cometidos nos dois episódios e pede apuração sobre suspeita de grupo armado no campus. Marcinho Belota (PL) e Athally Albuquerque devem ser interrogados.
articles.summary: Promotoria possíveis crimes cometidos nos dois episódios e pede apuração sobre suspeita de grupo armado no campus. Marcinho Belota (PL) e Athally devem ser ouvidos.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público Eleitoral (MPE) reforçou o pedido de investigação por parte da Polícia Federal (PF) no caso das invasões à Universidade Federal de Roraima (UFRR) envolvendo políticos em Boa Vista . O órgão pediu oficialmente o interrogatório de Marcinho Belota (PL) e Athally Albuquerque (Republicanos), além da apuração de cinco possíveis crimes cometidos no campus Paricarana.

Entenda🔎: Na última sexta-feira (16), a invasão no bloco de Direito envolveu o deputado estadual e a blogueira de direita , que rasgaram panfletos de estudantes. Já no sábado (17), um outro grupo , suspeito de estar armado , entrou na instituição, interrompeu aulas, intimidou servidoras e também retirou cartazes.

De acordo com o MPE, as condutas dos políticos e do grupo que invadiu o Centro de Ciências Humanas (CCH) no dia seguinte, podem configurar crimes . A lista inclui constrangimento ilegal , dano qualificado , perturbação do serviço público , possível porte ilegal de arma e usurpação de função pública (quando alguém age como autoridade de fiscalização sem ter o cargo para isso).

Para avançar nas investigações, o promotor de Justiça Eleitoral Marco Antônio Bordin pediu que a PF interrogue Belota , Athally e os homens envolvidos na segunda invasão , que já foram identificados pela Polícia Militar .

Em nota , o deputado Marcinho Belota declarou estar "ansioso" pelo início das investigações. "Já que segundo ele [MPE] existiu destruição de panfletos, alguém fez. E se alguém fez é sinal que está assumindo a culpa de criar fake News" , acrescentou o parlamentar em pronunciamento.

Os agentes também devem recolher imagens das câmeras de segurança e ouvir estudantes , professores e servidores que presenciaram os atos.

A reitoria da UFRR foi notificada pelo MPE . A universidade tem um prazo de cinco dias para explicar se havia autorização ou alguma regra interna que permitisse a distribuição e colagem dos panfletos feitos pelos alunos. O g1 solicitou um posicionamento à Universidade e aguarda resposta.

O MPE destacou que, antes da ação dos políticos, a UFRR já havia negado um pedido para retirar o material , por entender que a divulgação respeitava a legislação eleitoral.

Ação aconteceu no bloco de Direito da Universidade Federal de Roraima — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Na sexta-feira, Marcinho Belota e Athally entraram no Centro Acadêmico de Direito e rasgaram informativos feitos por universitários. Eles alegaram que os panfletos contra o candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) eram "fake news" .

Em notas enviadas ao g1 , o parlamentar e a blogueira negaram qualquer invasão e alegaram ter recebido orientação de um setor jurídico da universidade para verificar as denúncias no local.

Ocorrência envolveu um grupo de pessoas, policiais militares e servidores da UFRR, em Boa Vista. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

No dia seguinte, sábado, um segundo grupo com cerca de cinco pessoas entrou nos blocos de Direito e do Centro de Ciências Humanas (CCH). Eles interromperam aulas, hostilizaram servidores e arrancaram cartazes e uma bandeira de um movimento estudantil antifascista .

Testemunhas relataram que integrantes desse grupo estariam armados, o que motivou o pedido do MPE para que a PF investigue a fundo o porte ilegal de armas no campus. À PM, os homens alegaram na ocasião que estavam na universidade para "fiscalizar propaganda político-partidária" .

Devido às invasões, a UFRR repudiou os atos, classificados como intimidação e violência . Para proteger a comunidade acadêmica, a instituição solicitou reforço na segurança por parte da própria PF, da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF) e da Força Nacional.

articles.title: Ahead of Accession Day, UK MPs move motion to reaffirm India's sovereignty over J&K
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A group of British MPs are aiming to reaffirm India's sovereignty over Jammu and Kashmir in a motion tabled ahead of Accession Day on October
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A group of British MPs are aiming to reaffirm India's sovereignty over Jammu and Kashmir in a motion tabled ahead of Accession Day on October 26. The motion also raises concerns over terrorism in the region, including targeted killings of Kashmiri Pandits.Sponsored by Conservative MP Bob Blackman, the Early Day Motion marks the anniversary of Maharaja Hari Singh signing the Instrument of Accession in 1947. It calls for respect for sovereign boundaries in discussions on Jammu and Kashmir, while noting that Kashmiri Pandits continue to face threats of terrorism and intimidation, reported ANI.The motion expresses sympathy for civilians killed and injured in terrorist attacks across Jammu and Kashmir, including Pakistan-occupied regions. It also highlights casualties among security personnel and civilians, placing the security situation alongside calls for constructive dialogue and community cohesion.On India-UK ties, the motion stresses the importance of strong bilateral relations. It also acknowledges the contribution of British communities of Jammu and Kashmiri heritage to the UK's cultural, social and civic life.The motion welcomes peaceful Accession Day commemorations in Britain, saying such events can promote historical awareness, cultural exchange and civic participation.Blackman, who represents Harrow East, signed the motion on October 12. Democratic Unionist Party MP Jim Shannon and Labour MP Gill Furniss signed it on October 13.An Early Day Motion allows MPs to place their views on the parliamentary record and invite other lawmakers to support them. articles.title: In 1886, Thomas Edison bought Glenmont for his wife Mina; the 15-acre New Jersey estate is now the only National Park Service-owned home in a 420-acre private community
articles.summary: In 1886, Thomas Edison purchased Glenmont, a 15-acre estate in New Jersey’s Llewellyn Park, as a home for his new wife, Mina Miller.
articles.body: In 1886, Thomas Edison purchased Glenmont, a 15-acre estate in New Jersey’s Llewellyn Park, as a home for his new wife, Mina Miller. More than a century later, the property remains distinct within the private residential community, which spans 420 acres and contains more than 170 private homes. According to the National Park Service (NPS), Glenmont is the only home in the community owned by the agency. Built in 1880, the estate later became a family home and is now preserved alongside Edison’s laboratory as part of Thomas Edison National Historical Park. Its history also reflects the household and family life of one of America’s best-known inventorsHow Llewellyn Park became a private community in 1857Glenmont is situated within Llewellyn Park, a private residential community that was marketed as “Country Homes for City People” in 1857. According to the NPS, the community was designed as a country retreat for intellectuals and businessmen, with large residential plots and winding roads. Its layout also incorporated a 50-acre preserved woodland known as The Ramble, intended for the shared enjoyment of residents. These features formed part of the community’s original design and distinguished it as a planned residential development.The community’s early rules governed both its buildings and access to the grounds. The NPS audio tour explains that the original deed prohibited properties from being used as a hotel, slaughterhouse, brewery, distillery or hat factory. Visitors initially needed calling cards to enter through the main gate, although the requirement was relaxed in 1873 to allow respectable strangers and visitors to enter without one. The NPS states that Llewellyn Park remains a private residential community, governed by its deed of trust and managed by a committee of managers elected by the proprietors.How Glenmont became the only National Park Service-owned homeThe National Park Service identifies Glenmont as the only property it owns within Llewellyn Park, a community covering 420 acres. Its audio tour describes the Edison estate as one of more than 170 private homes in the community. The transcript states: “The Edison’s 15-acre estate is one of over a hundred and seventy private homes in the 420-acre community, and the only one owned by the National Park Service.” This distinction separates Glenmont’s ownership from that of the surrounding privately held residential properties.The estate’s status is connected to the preservation of Edison’s home and its contents. According to the NPS audio tour, Mina Edison sold the estate to TAE Inc. in 1946, a year before her death, on the condition that Glenmont and its contents be preserved as a memorial to her husband and his work. The National Park Service has administered the site alongside Edison’s laboratory on Main Street since 1959. The agency’s stewardship has kept the house within the wider historic site dedicated to commemorating Edison’s work and achievements.Thomas Edison’s family life at Glenmont after moving in 1886Glenmont served as the home of Thomas and Mina Edison and their family. When the couple moved into the estate after their marriage in 1886, it also became home to Edison’s three children from his first marriage: Marion, Thomas Jr and William Leslie. The NPS records that Edison called Marion and Thomas Jr “Dot” and “Dash”, nicknames associated with his work on telegraph equipment. Edison and Mina later had three children together: Madeleine, born in 1888; Charles, born in 1890; and Theodore, born in 1898.The grounds also contained facilities that supported the household, including a garage, barn, greenhouse, potting shed and gardens. The family grew fruits and vegetables and kept chickens and cows, although the estate was not completely self-sufficient. Glenmont was also linked to Edison’s nearby laboratory: the house was wired for electricity in 1887, and underground wires were installed to connect it to the laboratory. Edison died at Glenmont on 18 October 1931, while Mina continued to live there until she died in 1947. In 1963, at the family’s request, their remains were moved from Rosedale Cemetery in Orange to the Glenmont estate.Therefore, document Glenmont as both the former home of the Edison family and a property preserved within a private residential community. Its 15-acre grounds form part of the 420-acre Llewellyn Park, where it remains the only home owned by the National Park Service.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Injured Bend, Oregon, teacher tried to shut classroom door during school shooting before playing dead
articles.summary: A Silver Rail Elementary teacher described being shot at close range and pretending to be dead as the Bend, Oregon, school shooting unfolded.
articles.body: A teacher who was injured during last Thursday's school shooting in Bend, Oregon, said she tried to shut a classroom door before pretending to be dead in the hope that the gunman would not target her again. Becky Drury made the remarks in a statement released to the media on Wednesday, as the Bend Police Department confirmed that the firearm used in the attack on Silver Rail Elementary, which left three children and one teacher dead, was "purchased legally." "Here is what I remember: Once I realized something was happening outside, I ran to see what was going on. I then saw the shooter and immediately ran back into the classroom. I turned to shut the door behind me, but the shooter was already there. Before I could do anything more, he shot me at close range and I fell to the ground," Drury said. "Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured. I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else," she added. "So, I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again." HERO DAD WHO TOOK DOWN OREGON SCHOOL SHOOTER IDENTIFIED ALONG WITH TEACHER, STUDENT BOTH KILLED IN ATTACK Drury continued, "What happened in that classroom was unimaginable, and like so many in this community, my heart is broken for everyone affected by this tragedy," and her "thoughts are with those who were hurt, those we lost, their families, our school, and the Bend community." The Bend Police Department said on Wednesday that detectives are continuing a "complex investigation." "They have served search warrants at the shooting suspect's home, as well as on his electronic devices and his social media accounts on a variety of platforms. That work continues, and it takes time," the department said in a statement. BEND SCHOOL DISTRICT HONORS SLAIN TEACHER, PRAISES STAFF MEMBER'S COURAGE DURING ATTACK: 'FOREVER GRATEFUL' The 16-year-old shooter was "neutralized" by a good Samaritan, police said. Bend-La Pine Schools began welcoming students back to their other schools on Wednesday following the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary. articles.title: Marine life on the brink? 96% of coral reefs could face collapse by 2075
articles.summary: Almost all of the world's shallow-water coral reef ecosystems could face collapse by 2075, as rising ocean temperatures and increasingly severe marine
articles.body: Almost all of the world's shallow-water coral reef ecosystems could face collapse by 2075, as rising ocean temperatures and increasingly severe marine heatwaves push some of the planet's richest marine habitats towards a critical tipping point.According to a global assessment by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), 96 percent of shallow-water coral reef ecosystems face a critical risk of collapse when projected climate change impacts are taken into account.The findings were announced on the sidelines of a United Nations biodiversity conference in Albania on Thursday, with the IUCN warning that warming oceans and marine heatwaves are pushing coral reef ecosystems towards collapse.The assessment's scientific lead, Mishal Gudka, said the escalating threat should serve as a warning to accelerate conservation efforts rather than trigger despair.“The risk of coral reef collapse is escalating, but this must be a wake-up call rather than a cause for despair,” Gudka said.IUCN director-general Grethel Aguilar also stressed the importance of coral reefs as an indicator of ocean health, warning that their deterioration threatens ecosystems and communities that depend on them.“Coral reefs are one of the clearest vital signs of the ocean’s health,” Aguilar said.The assessment identified climate change as the “single most consistent threat driving coral reef decline worldwide”, with rising sea temperatures and marine heatwaves accelerating the deterioration of reef ecosystems.It covered 127 tropical and subtropical ecoregions and approximately 188,362 square kilometres of coral reefs globally, examining the threats that could undermine their long-term survival.The threat extends to some of the world's best-known reef systems, including Australia's Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle in Southeast Asia and the western Pacific, the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System and the Red Sea coral reefs.The assessment placed these major reef systems among those facing critical levels of risk, raising concerns over the future of marine biodiversity and the communities that depend on these habitats.Mishal Gudka, the scientific lead of the assessment, cautioned that the findings should not be interpreted as an inevitable end for all coral reefs.“Coral reefs have shown a remarkable ability to bounce back from devastating bleaching events,” Gudka said. “Pockets of surviving, resilient coral reefs can still remain in the future, so we must do everything within our reach to set them up for success.”Coral reefs, often described as the “rainforests of the sea”, support around a quarter of marine species and are among the world's richest ecosystems in terms of biodiversity. They provide food and livelihoods through fisheries and tourism, while acting as natural barriers that reduce wave energy and help protect coastlines from erosion and storms.The IUCN assessment warned that when a reef ecosystem collapses, living hard corals disappear and are replaced by algae, rubble and sponges.This transformation reduces the habitat available to reef fish and other marine organisms, undermining the ecosystem's ability to sustain biodiversity and support coastal communities.

articles.title: Florida wildlife officials confirm an established Burmese python population in Charlotte County, beyond the snakes’ historic Everglades stronghold
articles.summary: Florida's invasive Burmese pythons have moved into new territory, and state wildlife officials have now confirmed the move.
articles.body: Florida's invasive Burmese pythons have moved into new territory, and state wildlife officials have now confirmed the move. The snakes are considered established in Charlotte County, in south-west Florida, well outside the Everglades region that has long been the centre of the problem. The finding matters beyond one county, because it shows these giant constrictors can form breeding colonies far from their historic stronghold. Conservationists and wildlife managers are weighing what the discovery means for native animals, for nearby communities and for the costly, decades-long effort to limit a species that has proved extremely hard to find, let alone remove.Wildlife officials confirm an established Burmese python population in western Charlotte CountyThe Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission says Burmese pythons were historically centred in Everglades National Park in Miami-Dade County. They later became established from Lake Okeechobee to Key Largo, and from western Broward County west to Collier County. A new satellite population has since emerged. A commission spokesperson told ABC that the snakes are considered established in a portion of western Charlotte County, north of Naples and Fort Myers on the Gulf Coast. The agency began receiving more python reports in 2020, mostly from the townships of Rotonda West, Placida, Englewood East and South Gulf Cove.Escaped or released captive snakes, not natural migration, are the likely source of the new colonyThe commission says there is no indication that the pythons reached Charlotte County through natural migration. It believes they were most likely captive animals that escaped or were released. The wider history points the same way. The United States Fish and Wildlife Service estimates that about 180,000 Burmese pythons were brought into the country between 1975 and 2018, and many entered the ecosystem through accidental or deliberate release. By 2000, the species had a self-sustaining breeding population in South Florida.Burmese pythons are apex predators whose appetite leaves native wildlife and ecosystems at riskBurmese pythons feed on opossums, alligators, birds and other animals, including prey larger than themselves. Ian Bartoszek, a wildlife biologist at the Conservancy of Southwest Florida in Naples, and Robert McCleery, a wildlife ecologist at the University of Florida, both told ABC News why the spread worries them. Bartoszek said the snake is a generalist apex predator, which is why there is such interest in removing it from the ecosystem. McCleery said that once pythons move in, most mammal populations are decimated, leaving a "simplified ecosystem" dominated by rodents and other invasive species. He added that nobody has yet found a way to stop or reverse that pattern at the scale needed. Newsweek reported that, according to the commission, observations of some mammals, such as raccoons and bobcats, fell by 95 per cent in Everglades National Park after the snakes became established.Low detection rates mean experts cannot estimate how many Burmese pythons live in Florida todayCounting the snakes is a challenge in itself. The commission says wildlife experts have been unable to put a figure on the total because the animals are so hard to detect. Research puts the chance of spotting one at between 1 per cent and 3 per cent, meaning a survey area holding 100 snakes might turn up only one to three. In Everglades National Park, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service says searchers find roughly one python for every eight hours of looking.Surveys continue in Charlotte and Lee counties while Florida's Python Challenge offers cash prizesThe commission and its partner agencies are continuing to monitor and survey for Burmese pythons in Charlotte and Lee counties. Removal remains the main tool. Newsweek reported that more than 27,000 pythons have been taken out of the Florida environment since 2000, and that a single female can lay more than 100 eggs, which makes control difficult once a population takes hold. This year's Florida Python Challenge, which ran from 10 to 19 July, offered a $25,000 prize pool across designated South Florida public lands, with a $10,000 grand prize for the participant who removed the most snakes. The 2025 challenge removed a record 294 pythons from the Everglades ecosystem.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Trump is trying ‘The Art of the Deal’ in Ukraine but what must Putin give up?
articles.summary: Washington Post reports White House holds up Patriot interceptor transfers to Ukraine while Russian missiles keep falling on Ukrainian cities.
articles.body: Russian missiles keep falling on Ukrainian cities while Washington holds up approval of Patriot interceptor transfers to Ukraine, according to The Washington Post. A Ukrainian official told the Post that only "a couple" of interceptors remained. President Donald Trump wants this war to end, and that goal deserves support. But a deal that squeezes only Ukraine is not a peace plan, and right now Kyiv absorbs the pressure while Moscow collects the relief. Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged on Oct. 20 that a batch bought for Kyiv may not have been delivered, but he rejected any political motive. "There's nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine," he said. So is Washington protecting scarce supplies, applying negotiating pressure or both? Americans deserve an answer, including what concessions Washington expects from Russian President Vladimir Putin. TRUMP RUSSIA DEAL COULD FUEL PUTIN'S WAR, EX-NATO COMMANDER WARNS AS ZELENSKYY SAYS 'NYET' The administration's strongest defense is scarcity, so start with the missiles. Lockheed Martin delivered 620 PAC-3 MSE interceptors in 2025 and plans to expand annual capacity to 2,000 over seven years. The Iran war compounded the problem. A July assessment by the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that heavy combat use had pushed American Patriot inventories below 1,000. UKRAINE'S ZELENSKYY OPEN TO FREEZING FRONT LINES IN CEASEFIRE WITH RUSSIA A president must keep enough interceptors to protect American troops. Having worked on military strategy and security cooperation at the Pentagon, I take that obligation seriously. Ukraine's needs cannot erase our responsibilities elsewhere. European money does not change that math. Kiel Institute data covering the first half of 2026 identify Europe as the largest military-aid donor, yet American stockpiles supplied more than 90% of the aid delivered through NATO's Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL). Europe is paying American industry to arm Ukraine, and Washington controls the tap. AMERICA FACES A CRISIS IN OUR MILITARY ARSENAL THAT TRUMP IS RACING TO FIX The lasting answer to scarcity is production. When U.S. Sens. Roger Wicker, R-Miss., and Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv Oct. 9, he pressed for faster Patriot production licensing and offered joint production of interceptors. Washington should pursue it, with technology safeguards. Still, scarcity does not explain every pending decision, and Washington owes the allies who paid for these weapons a straight explanation. Nor does it explain the broader pressure on Kyiv. TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA The clearest example involves the same pipeline. Reuters reports that Washington threatened to stop the allied-funded PURL weapons pipeline to press Kyiv to halt its deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. That is leverage over Ukrainian military operations, not proof of a coordinated campaign to remove Zelenskyy. The satellite dispute is murkier. Blamed for throttling Ukraine's terminals, billionaire Elon Musk posted that limits "are decided by the U.S. military and ultimately" by the president. Reuters then traced the restriction to the White House through unnamed officials. Trump denied it. "It wasn't us," he told reporters Oct. 16. Separately, Ukraine went three days without American missile warnings before Zelenskyy said Oct. 18 that intelligence sharing had resumed. ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE The pressure is also personal. Trump called Oct. 10 for Ukraine to replace its president. Yet Zelenskyy sat down with American envoys in Oslo on Oct. 20. A leader who shows up for talks is not refusing diplomacy. The administration's strongest defense is scarcity, so start with the missiles. Lockheed Martin delivered 620 PAC-3 MSE interceptors in 2025 and plans to expand annual capacity to 2,000 over seven years. Now consider the other side of the ledger. Trump announced an energy ceasefire Oct. 11, although Russian agreement remained unclear. A week later, Russian strikes hit 28 substations and other energy facilities, according to the Institute for the Study of War, leaving roughly 550,000 Ukrainian households without power. Kyiv was pressed to stop hitting refineries while Moscow kept hitting the grid. Putin never confirmed the ceasefire, and his missiles show he never intended to honor it. TRUMP TRIES DIFFERENT APPROACH WITH RUSSIA TO BRING AMERICANS RELIEF AMID ONGOING WAR WITH UKRAINE Moscow, meanwhile, received relief. On Oct. 9, Treasury issued a license authorizing specified Russian diesel transactions. Reuters later reported that Washington hoped the diesel deal would soften Moscow's negotiating position. The administration's case is domestic. Diesel hit a record $6.52 a gallon in September as the Iran war choked the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump promised relief for farmers, ranchers and truckers. But Lawfare's analysis found the agreed Russian exports would cover about 2% of American demand. The price relief is speculative. Moscow's gains are not: sanctions relief and American pressure on Kyiv to spare Russian refineries. PENTAGON RACES TO BUY 10X MORE MISSILES AS IRAN WAR DWINDLES ARSENAL, THREATENS READINESS FOR CHINA AGGRESSION Offering an adversary an incentive can be sound diplomacy. The question is what the incentive buys. So far, the bombing has not stopped. Nor has softer treatment softened the Kremlin's terms. When Zelenskyy offered a 60-day ceasefire to permit elections, the Kremlin rejected it on Oct. 12, saying it wanted an overall settlement. Moscow refused the very pause that Trump's call for new Ukrainian leadership would require. Putin's ambitions run larger still. The New York Post reports that he wants a summit with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to settle the war without Zelenskyy or Europe at the table, a redux of Yalta. Putin bargains as if time is on his side. The battlefield says otherwise. Reuters reported Oct. 17 that Russian advances had slowed and many front lines remained largely static. That gives Washington room to demand reciprocity. Wicker, the Senate Armed Services Committee chairman, proposed one approach on Oct. 18: Ukrainian restraint against petroleum facilities in exchange for American targeting assistance against Russian missile launches. It deserves consideration. But Putin would still need to offer restraint of his own. So what must Putin give up? As I argued in these pages last December, a durable agreement requires credible enforcement, and enforcement begins with concessions Moscow can be held to. Russia must halt strikes on Ukraine's power grid and cities, the same restraint Washington demanded of Kyiv. It must accept monitored ceasefire terms, defined restrictions on military activity and consequences for violations. It must negotiate with Kyiv, not over Kyiv's head in China. And it must recognize that the size of Ukraine's army and the choice of its security partners belong to Kyiv, not the Kremlin. For his part, Trump should preserve American reserves, expand production, insist on European performance and refuse any summit that decides Ukraine's fate without Ukraine. Diesel licenses and any further sanctions relief should depend on compliance, with automatic snap-back penalties if Moscow cheats. articles.title: French weekend protests to be limited to union demos only, says Macron
articles.summary: Some cities including Lyon and Nice have banned all protests, and the French president said only authorised demos would be allowed.
articles.body:
Only authorised union protests will be allowed in French towns and cities on Saturday, President Emmanuel Macron has said, after demonstrations across the country turned violent last weekend.

Speaking as some cities including Lyon and Nice imposed complete bans, Macron said "illegitimate" protests would not be allowed but unions would be offered alternative routes so that businesses could be protected.

Big demonstrations against the high cost of living and school conditions were overshadowed last Saturday by riots and looting that saw business and historic buildings destroyed.

Interior Minister Jean-Didier Berger said police deployments would be increased by 20% compared to last weekend, after the government was accused of being blindsided by the scale of the unrest.

France's justice minister said on Thursday that 217 people had been jailed over last weekend's disorder after being convicted in fast-track trials, with that number expected to rise.

Gérald Darmanin said 2,700 people had been arrested across France and more than 1,000 have appeared in court.

Half of those detained had no prior criminal record, he said, according to Le Figaro newspaper.

Macron met intelligence services and ministers on Thursday, to prepare for the next national day of protests on Saturday.

"The general recommendation is that there should be no demonstrations. Those who want to continue to demonstrate, when they are trade union organisations, will have alternative routes proposed by the prefects," the French president announced. "When they're not union organisations, wherever possible, they'll be banned."

He attacked what he called "political and even seditious acts organised by far-left groups that aim to bring down the Republic".

Curfews were imposed in several cities in the aftermath of the weekend rioting, and Macron said the government wanted a return to calm.

The gilets jaunes (yellow-vest) movement was behind many of last weekend's protests and Paris authorities have said several of their proposed marches have been banned.

In Lyon, France's third-biggest city, regional authorities have imposed a blanket ban on demonstrations.

"In light of the mobilisation that is circulating and in view of the events of 17 October, the prefect has decided to prohibit by decree any demonstration in the city of Lyon this Saturday," the Rhône prefecture said in a statement.

Similar announcements have been made in Toulon on the south coast, the centre of Rouen in the north-west, and Grenoble in the east.

Partial curfews variously restricting the movement of young people and gatherings have been in place this week in cities including Marseille, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon in the south as well as Lille and other towns in the north.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu promised a "massive" deployment of police officers this week to deal with any unrest this weekend, but some officers have told French media they are not trained to deal with large crowds.

Around 550,000 people took part in demonstrations on 17 October to protest rising fuel prices and the cost of living, which have escalated after weeks of student protests .

Marches were largely peaceful and took place in several major French cities, including Paris, backed by unions, gilets jaunes and student groups. But they were marred by scenes of violence, looting and destruction.

Lyon's tourism office was set on fire by demonstrators during last weekend's protests.

Mayor Grégory Doucet said the burning of the office, housed in a 19th-Century building, was "a tragedy".

In the city of Limoges, the clock tower and parts of the roof of the ornate city hall were engulfed in flames before collapsing on Saturday.

A second suspect aged 66 was arrested on Thursday, after a man in his 30s was detained on suspicion of the attempted murder of police officers who were in the city hall when the fire started.

The iconic Place de la République was vandalised in the capital, Paris, when groups of rioters took over parts of the city, wreaking havoc.

Following the unrest, France's interior minister Laurent Nuñez tendered his resignation, which was rejected by President Macron.

The Élysée Palace asked him instead to look at how to make France's streets safer and bring rioters to justice.

Nuñez said his teams had forecast 200,000 demonstrators, a figure much lower than the 550,000 estimated to have gathered.

The unrest has come as Macron enters the final months of his presidency, with elections scheduled for 18 April and 1 May next year.

articles.title: Teacher in Oregon shooting said she pretended to be dead to survive
articles.summary: The teacher said she could not help children because she was badly injured by the attacker.
articles.body:
Some readers may find this article distressing.

A 54-year-old teacher who survived a mass shooting at an Oregon elementary school said she pretended to be dead so the gunman would not shoot her again.

Becky Drury, a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School, said in a statement shared with US media that as she tried to shut her classroom door, the gunman shot her and she fell to the floor.

"I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again," Drury said.

The attacker - who has been identified as a 16-year-old former student at the school - killed three students and a teacher before a parent from the school fatally shot him.

In her first remarks since the 15 October shooting in Bend, Oregon, Drury said that she went to see what was happening outside the special-education classroom, and after spotting the shooter, she tried to shut the door.

The attacker still managed to shoot her, so she could not help any of the children in the classroom.

"Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured," she said. "I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else."

Drury suffered serious but not life-threatening harm from the shooting, which killed five-year-old Rhoam Summer, an eight and eleven-year-old, and 25-year-old teacher Megan Lambert.

Police have said another teacher - who has not been named - attempted to disarm the gunman by throwing her mobile phone. She was not injured.

A father of two other children who had followed the suspect into the school then shot and killed the attacker, who officials named as Griffin J John II.

Reports had emerged that another teacher threw herself on top of a student to protect the child during the shooting, but Drury said she wanted to clear the record about what happened on 15 October.

"I know there has been contradictory reporting about my actions that day, but the truth is I was shot before I had any chance to act," she said in her statement.

Police have not yet shared a motive for the suspect, who officials say was a special-education needs student at Silver Rail.

Drury said what happened in the classroom was "unimaginable".

"[L]ike so many in this community, my heart is broken for everyone affected by this tragedy," she said.

articles.title: Caroline Flack's brother never recovered, inquest hears
articles.summary: Paul Flack was "everyone's favourite person" but this "took its toll", an inquest hears.
articles.body:
The brother of TV presenter Caroline Flack took his own life having "never recovered" after his sister's death, an inquest heard.

Paul Flack, 55, was found unresponsive at his home in Sandringham Road, Norwich, on 21 June, and died later in hospital.

His partner told Norfolk Coroner's Court how he had struggled with his father developing dementia and his younger sister's death in 2020.

Area Coroner Johanna Thompson gave a narrative conclusion, stating Paul Flack died while under the influence of alcohol and that his "intent in doing so is unknown".

He was described as "everyone's favourite person" by his partner Joanna Millington, but she said this "took its toll".

His sister, the ex-Love Island and X Factor host, was found dead at her home in Stoke Newington, east London, on 15 February 2020.

"We then went into lockdown for Covid," said Millington, who provided a written statement to the court.

"I do not think Paul ever recovered from this."

An inquest later established Caroline Flack took her own life , aged 40, having feared press intrusion ahead of her trial accused of assaulting her boyfriend.

Earlier, the inquest heard Paul Flack sought help for low mood from his GP in August 2020, but he did not attend follow-up appointments or counselling.

The self-employed graphic designer also struggled to find work as the "industry had begun to decline", which "contributed to his sadness", his partner of 32 years said.

His father Ian developed dementia in his early 70s in recent years, and died at the beginning of this year.

Millington added: "[Paul] was a lovely person, he took a lot on from everyone.

"There was no suggestion he would ever harm himself, he said he never would."

On the day of Paul Flack's death - which was Father's Day - the inquest heard he and Millington enjoyed some time together as a family.

At 18:30 BST, his daughter offered him a cup of tea and a slice of cake she had made.

He declined and instead went to the shop and bought four beers and spent the rest of the evening in the garden listening to music while his partner and daughter watched a film inside.

Will Caroline Flack's death be a turning point?

Before going to bed at about 22:20, his daughter found he was no longer in the hammock outside.

She screamed when she then found him unresponsive.

A neighbour attempted CPR and another neighbour called an ambulance.

The coroner heard Millington told a neighbour he had been in a "bad mood all day" and that it may be because they were celebrating Father's Day so soon after his dad's death.

He was pronounced dead at Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital at 23:45.

A toxicology report found he had a blood alcohol level four times over the legal alcohol limit to drive.

Paul Flack was born in Enfield in north London, but his family later moved to Norwich, where he lived much of his life. He had two children.

No family members were present at the inquest

articles.title: In 2018, two New York women raised $12,500 to erase $1.5 million in medical debt; 1,284 strangers received yellow envelopes confirming their bills were forgiven
articles.summary: In 2018, two women in Ithaca, New York, set out to help people struggling with unpaid medical bills, although neither had the means to pay off large debts
articles.body: In 2018, two women in Ithaca, New York, set out to help people struggling with unpaid medical bills, although neither had the means to pay off large debts individually. As reported by The New York Times, Judith Jones, a retired chemist, and Carolyn Kenyon, a psychoanalyst, organised a local fundraising campaign and collected $12,500 over several months. They sent the money to a nonprofit that buys overdue medical bills for a fraction of their face value before cancelling them. The contribution enabled the organisation to acquire a portfolio worth $1.5 million in medical debt, benefiting 1,284 New Yorkers who had no prior connection to the two women. For those recipients, the relief arrived in the form of an unexpected letter.How $12,500 grew into $1.5 million in medical debt reliefJones and Kenyon became involved in the initiative after learning about R.I.P. Medical Debt, a New York-based nonprofit established to help people burdened by medical bills. Both women belonged to the Finger Lakes chapter of the Campaign for New York Health, an organisation advocating universal health coverage through the proposed New York Health Act.Their fundraising effort began in the spring of 2018. Rather than attempt to cover individual patients' bills themselves, they collected donations from people willing to contribute towards buying existing medical debt. By the end of the summer, they had raised $12,500 and passed the money to the charity, which used it to purchase a portfolio of outstanding accounts.Medical debts that have remained unpaid for long periods can be sold to collection agencies and other buyers at steep discounts. Reportedly, R.I.P. Medical Debt used this system to purchase the $1.5 million portfolio for roughly half a cent for every dollar owed. The people whose bills were included did not have to apply to Jones and Kenyon for assistance. The charity selected eligible accounts and arranged for the balances to be forgiven.How the campaign erased unpaid medical bills across New York StateThe result reached households across New York State in November 2018. About 1,300 yellow envelopes were sent to residents whose medical debts had been acquired and cancelled through the campaign. According to the New York Times, the 1,284 recipients lived in 40 of New York's 62 counties, with the affected accounts linked to around 130 hospitals and their branches. The debts covered people who had received medical care but had not been able to settle their bills.They had not necessarily known their accounts were being considered for relief, and the forgiveness was provided without requiring them to repay the donors. According to the charity, the cancelled debts were treated as gifts and removed from recipients' credit reports.How the nonprofit made donations go furtherR.I.P. Medical Debt was founded in 2014 by Craig Antico and Jerry Ashton, both of whom had previously worked in the debt collection industry. Their experience had brought them into contact with people who struggled to pay old bills, including debts arising from medical treatment.The organisation adopted a different approach to the accounts it acquired. Instead of pursuing borrowers for payment, it raised money to purchase qualifying debts and cancel them. Because overdue accounts can be sold for a small proportion of their original value, relatively modest donations can cover balances worth much more on paper. The charity focused its work on people facing financial hardship. Its stated criteria included individuals earning less than twice the federal poverty level, those experiencing serious economic difficulties and people facing insolvency.A television fundraiser had already drawn attentionThe charity had attracted national attention two years earlier, when British comedian John Oliver featured medical debt in an episode of his HBO programme Last Week Tonight in 2016. As part of the segment, Oliver paid $60,000 to purchase and forgive $14.9 million in medical debt through the organisation. Around 9,000 people received letters informing them that their debts had been cancelled as a result of that effort. The broadcast introduced a wider audience to the mechanics of buying debt portfolios and showed how donations could be used to clear balances far beyond the amount contributed.Other fundraising campaigns followed, including efforts involving NBC and Telemundo affiliates. By the time Jones and Kenyon's campaign was reported in December 2018, R.I.P. Medical Debt said its work had forgiven $434 million in medical debt and assisted approximately 250,000 people. Those figures were substantial, but they represented only a small portion of the problem the organisation was addressing. The charity estimated that Americans held more than $750 billion in past-due medical debt.Relief for individuals, not a solution to medical costsThe scale of the wider problem was part of the reason Jones and Kenyon approached their campaign as a limited intervention. Their fundraising could not change the price of hospital care or resolve the financial pressures that had left people with unpaid bills. It could, however, remove some existing obligations. For Antico, the value of the programme lay partly in the fact that recipients did not need to seek help publicly. The charity could identify eligible accounts, purchase them and arrange for the debt to be cancelled before the affected individuals knew what had happened.The yellow envelopes sent out in November were the final stage of the Ithaca campaign. Jones and Kenyon had raised $12,500; the charity had turned that contribution into the cancellation of $1.5 million in medical debt. For 1,284 people across New York, the outcome was a letter confirming that money they had owed for medical care was no longer due.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: FIFA’s Infantino made to wait on Asian support as chief coy at AFC session
articles.summary: ‘We’re not against anyone and we’re not in favour of anyone,’ says AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa.
articles.body:
The president of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) gave no hint about the body’s support — or opposition — to the re-election of Gianni Infantino as FIFA president.

The votes of the AFC’s 47 members could be critical when Infantino seeks his fourth term as the head of global football’s governing body in an election in March. Infantino faces strong opposition in Europe, and has staunch support in Africa — and Asia could provide the swing votes.

Opposition candidates have until November 18 to file. So far, none have

“For people who try to divide us, this is not going to happen,” AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa said on Thursday in a brief address to close a two-day session in Tokyo.

He gave no indication that the AFC as a body would take a position on Infantino.

That differed from just over two months ago, when the AFC joined the football governing bodies in North and Central America and Europe in saying Infantino committed a “fundamental breach of trust”.

Recent reports and his short talk on Thursday indicate Sheikh Salman may have moderated his views. Asia appears split. Qatar, the host of the 2022 World Cup, has come out in support of Infantino while Jordan has declared its opposition.

“We’re not against anyone and we’re not in favour of anyone,” Sheikh Salman said.

“We’re always going to express our feelings and try to do what’s best and what’s right for football. Not just in Asia.”

Recent AFC meetings in a five-star hotel in Tokyo were closed to the media. The conference was shown on the football confederation’s YouTube channel, and presentations were orchestrated without reporters present.

Infantino seldom speaks with the media. He has been travelling and electioneering in Asia, but did not appear publicly at the seminars in Tokyo. During the week, FIFA’s media office promoted his presence in Bhutan and Bangladesh, which have small federations that each have one vote — the same as powerful football nations such as Spain and France.

Infantino apologised last week in Zurich to FIFA’s 37-member ruling council — which he chairs — for “mistakes” he made in assembling a now-scrapped $4.2bn selloff plan for the World Cup.

An Associated Press tally shows 87 of the 211 federations have indicated support for Infantino, either in individual comments or by endorsing statements of support by their regional confederations.

Sheikh Salman made passing reference to the turmoil in the Middle East and its effect on football in the region.

“We know that the world is changing and football, I think, gets affected as well from what’s happening,” he said, “whether it’s political, economic, or whatever it is.

“People are following the news, what’s happening in the Middle East. It’s important for us.”

The Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January is going ahead despite deadly attacks in the country by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, said Muhammed Q Alghamdi, a spokesman for the organising committee. There is a rising fear of an escalation in hostilities.

The Asian Cup is set for January 7 to February 5, with 24 teams playing matches in three cites — Riyadh, Jeddah, and Khobar. Reports suggest it may be too late to seek an alternative venue.

“I’d like to start by acknowledging that we are monitoring the regional developments and we’re working closely with our counterparts at the AFC to make sure we can provide an exceptional tournament,” Alghamdi said.

“I stand before you now, and I am pleased to say that daily life is ongoing in Saudi Arabia. Our job is to be ready, and we will be ready.”
