articles.title: Farmers protest in Trichy demanding loan waiver, govt assures action
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu farmers protest in Trichy seeking full cooperative crop loan waiver; police detain protesters, govt assures improved waiver plan after Chennai talks.
articles.body: Trichy: Hundreds of farmers from various associations in Tamil Nadu held a protest at Samayapuram near Trichy on Thursday, demanding a complete waiver of cooperative crop loans. They withdrew the agitation after the state government assured that their demands would be considered following a meeting held in Chennai.The protest resumed after five days of agitation in September, during which ministers had held talks with the associations and sought 20 days to examine the feasibility of a full loan waiver.With no significant progress on those assurances, farmers began gathering in large numbers at Samayapuram on Thursday. Police were deployed in strength as the protesters occupied the national highway.Initially, police attempted to pacify the farmers. However, as they were firm on protesting, police arrested the farmers by force and took them to a private hall. During detention, the protesters refused the food served by the police and insisted on talks specifically on the crop loan waiver. Meanwhile, police began stopping vehicles carrying groups of farmers at important points to prevent them from arriving in Samayapuram.Later in the evening, a group of ministers - Aadhav Arjuna (public works), N Anand (water resources), K A Sengottaiyan (revenue), M Vijay Balaji (handlooms), V Gandhiraj (cooperatives), R Vinoth (agriculture), S Ramesh (HR&CE) - and secretaries from various departments met representatives of the farmers’ associations at the Secretariat in Chennai.The ministers discussed the farmers’ grievances in detail and explained that government was already facing a fund crunch. articles.title: Bhavani devotee dies in bus accident 25 km from Vijayawada Kanaka Durga temple
articles.summary: Bhavani devotee Bonam Ammaji, 50, died after being hit by an APSRTC bus near Gannavaram, 25 km from Vijayawada’s Kanaka Durga temple.
articles.body: Vijayawada: In a tragic end to a 200-km spiritual journey, a 50-year-old Bhavani devotee from Kakinada district died in a road accident near Gannavaram on Thursday morning, just 25 km short of reaching Sri Kanaka Durga temple in Vijayawada.The deceased, identified as Bonam Ammaji, had set out on a pilgrimage on foot from Shankhavaram village in Kakinada district on Oct 15. She was undertaking the Pada Yatra to seek the blessings of Goddess Kanaka Durga.The accident occurred around 5 am near an HP petrol station opposite Vijayawada airport, as she approached Gannavaram on her way to the temple. According to preliminary information, an APSRTC bus, bearing number AP39 UX 4766, travelling from Eluru towards Vijayawada rammed into her from behind.Ammaji suffered severe head injuries in the collision and died instantly. Her death has cast a pall of gloom over the pilgrimage, which she had undertaken with the hope of completing the long walk and offering prayers at the hill shrine.The incident occurred when she was nearing the final stretch of her journey, having walked nearly 200 km from her native village. articles.title: PM Modi calls for stronger global institutions; takes ‘failed product’ jab at Congress
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and effective
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday called for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South and effective international cooperation during crises, while accusing the Congress leadership of repeatedly failing to launch its leader politically.Addressing the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi, PM Modi said institutions such as the United Nations were struggling to keep pace with the changing world order and emerging challenges, according to news agency ANI.PM Modi warned that trade, technology and sea routes were increasingly being “weaponised”, stressing the need for a global system that prevents the strong from exploiting the vulnerable. Citing ancient Indian statesman Chanakya, he referred to the Sanskrit aphorism ‘apranitah tu matsyanyayam udbhavayati’, which he explained as a situation where the absence of law and order allows the strong to prey on the weak.“The world does not need such a situation. It needs a system that stops this 'matsya nyaya' from happening,” PM Modi said.Highlighting India's role in global cooperation, Modi cited the country's humanitarian assistance during the Covid-19 pandemic. “During the Covid-19 pandemic, the world experienced India taking on such a role. India sent vaccines to every country in need; sent medicines to over 100 countries,” he said.“The changing world order calls for stronger global institutions, a greater voice for the Global South, and international cooperation that stands firm in times of crisis,” he added.PM Modi said India's vision of becoming a developed nation, or Viksit Bharat, by 2047 went beyond domestic ambitions. “It is also a guarantee for a better world,” he said, adding that international cooperation must remain effective during crises and not just in favourable circumstances. “India is strengthening its own capabilities to help strengthen the world,” he said.PM Modi targets Congress over repeated attempts to launch its leaderAt the same summit, PM Modi took a swipe at the Congress, accusing the party's leadership of becoming a burden on the organisation and repeatedly attempting to launch its leader politically.“This family of Congress has become a burden on its own party,” PM Modi said.Drawing a comparison with India's space programme, he said, “We don't have as many launches from Sriharikota in one year as the Congress makes failed attempts to launch its leader in one year.”Taking another dig at the opposition party, PM Modi questioned how long the country would remain at stake over these attempts. “Who knows how long Congress will keep the country at stake while trying to launch its ‘failed product’,” he said.PM Modi also accused some people of damaging India's global reputation and seeking foreign intervention in the country's affairs.“Some hell-bent on dragging India's reputation through mud; they go abroad, defame India, petition foreigners for intervention,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Germany target of 'intensive' espionage, Merz says after suspected Russian spy arrest
articles.summary: A Ukrainian man was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia - one of several such cases in Germany this year.
articles.body:
Germany is the target of "intensive" espionage activity, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said after a Ukrainian national was arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia.

Officials said the suspect, named as Vadym Y., had allegedly collected military-related intelligence from Germany.

Merz called the uncovering of the case a "success", but warned "let us not delude ourselves - the activities of Russian intelligence services in Germany remain at a consistently high level".

Several people alleged to be acting on behalf of Russia and other foreign powers have been arrested in Germany this year. Germany has been one of the leading European suppliers of weapons to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

The German Federal Prosecutor General's Office said on Thursday that Vadym Y., as he was identified under German privacy law, had been in contact with a Russian intelligence service through an intermediary since at least July 2025.

It also said the Ukrainian man had collected information including "on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition, and explosives".

He is due to appear before an investigating judge on Friday.

In January, a woman was arrested in Berlin suspected of gathering information for an intelligence officer at the Russian embassy.

Other arrests this year included a Romanian woman and a Ukrainian man accused of spying on an individual supplying drones from Germany to Ukraine, according to the prosecutor's office.

UK and Germany will face threats together, says Burnham in Berlin

Trial of German steakhouse heiress that sparked a huge spy scandal

Sabotage suspect held in Germany after spate of attacks on power grid

And, the former German spy chief August Hanning was arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power earlier this month. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.

Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.

Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D and accused him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents in exchange for money.

Speaking at the sidelines of a conference in Montenegro on Thursday, Merz said: "We will likely see more such cases in the coming months and years."

Merz reaffirmed a series of defence and security partnerships with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham earlier this month, including tackling hybrid attacks and hostile activity.

The talks between the two leaders came after Germany accused Russia of launching a drone fitted with explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport in September.

Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Germany of planting evidence to blame Russia.
